He was renowned for his mastery of the Way throughout Wu and Yue;
thus, a popular proverb praised him, saying:
"In the daylight at Xi, one can be refined and elegant."
The clarity of Yue is like ice and snow;
the loftiness of Hang touches the clouds and mists of heaven.
Having heard of their reputes, I admire those men.
Based on the popular proverb,
I have thus composed three stanzas of verse to expand upon its meaning.
Master Zhe’s prose is clear and elegant; Master Zhe’s prose is clear and elegant. Master Zhu’s writings are both pure and refined.
Heaven has bestowed such talent upon him that it cannot be rivaled.
Since ancient times, there have been monks who have excelled in literary composition.
The Venerable Xuzhuo emerged as the foremost during the Dayzao era;
though the transformations of creation shifted, his spirit did not migrate.
When Master Zhuo composed this poem, his mind was likewise so.
Above, he spans the *Sāo* and *Yā* styles; below, he sinks into the traditions of Sòng.
His brilliant thoughts range freely as his Way is perfected in its entirety.
When the Master of Chan cultivates literature, or when Xiū brushes his brush, it is by no means in vain.
He entices the human heart to penetrate the principles of the Buddha.
Gentry and scholars such as Lord Lu have long trodden the path of pure travel,
yearning for that which lies beyond the mundane world.
The person has passed away, but these words remain;
may the protection of the Dharma descend for ten thousand generations.
The clarity of Yue is like ice and snow; the clarity of Master Che is like ice and snow—Master Che’s purity is like ice and snow.
This eminent monk possessed a natural talent that set him apart from others.
By the age of thirty, his reputation as a poet was already established.
While his name resided among the ranks of poets, his heart remained fixed upon the Vinaya.
Not different from Huiyuan, yet distinct from Huixiu;
how could Jiaoran find his peer?
Amidst the drifting white clouds, where can they ever settle?
Suddenly entering Guanzhong, he sought out Bao and Li;
his solitary purity was difficult to establish amidst the opposition of the multitude,
yet in the end, he remained innocent amidst their slanderous words.
"When trees stand out above the forest, the wind will surely destroy them.
Master Che harbored such virtue that it became the seed of his own misfortune.
The ancients have already passed away; there is no more cause for lamentation."
I have composed this poem for you to bequeath to posterity.

The banner of Master Hang brushes the clouds and reaches the heavens; the banner of Master Hang brushes the clouds and reaches the heavens. This banner symbolizes the Master’s loftiness, which brushes the clouds and reaches the heavens.
Does it not lie in his virtue? How could it reside in mere silence?
Dwelling in solitude at the foot of a mountain hermitage,
he maintains a detached bearing, remaining aloof from the mundane world.
At times, he ascends the lofty cliffs in vain to gaze afar.
One does not hear his spoken words, but hears his pure whistling.
At that time, Lu Yu pursued profound inquiry;
he once entered the azure clouds and was privileged to hear the Way.
To summon rain to relieve drought and drive forth divine dragons—
how could this possibly be the same as human affairs?
It is the subtle mechanism that moves the sprouts of divergent minds.
This is why the Master praised Dao-biao.
[The Master] sent Zhang Biao-min, the Secretariat Official. One day, when the Master came to the mountain slopes, he said as he was departing:
"Where will you go after leaving me?"
The former commandant of Qingchen has also arrived; Zhou Gan and others come with him, their fine carriages and light jade pendants shimmering in brilliant array.
Upon entering the gate, he gazes at me with a gracious countenance;
we grasp each other’s sleeves beneath the trees as we follow one another.
Laughing and swaggering with unrestrained spirit and bold vigor,
he raised his head and did not notice the white sun slanting down.
He swept his mat and remained to lodge for the night within the rocky grotto.
Paper quilts and rush mats are indeed laughable;
yet, regardless of abundance or scarcity, one should simply choose what is suitable and beautiful.
With compliant silence, one neither speaks nor offers resistance.
At this time, in the middle of the second month of spring,
the long night lingers with a faint chill;
lofty discourse unfolds as refined interests converge.
Like a jar pouring into a spring, they vied with one another in profuse flow.
In a brief moment, they were summoned to sit together and declare their aspirations;
they spoke directly from the depths of their hearts, uttering pure and sincere words.
The minds of men differ as do their faces;
throughout their lives, each pursues their own ends.
Suddenly, Pyo-min hastened to the edge of his mat.
I say: My aspirations others do not know;
how could they be spoken of to those of shallow and vulgar customs?
Before I have even finished sucking my mother's breast, I already heave long sighs of lamentation.
From my youth, I followed a master to study the classics;
I did not explore the branches and leaves, but sought to exhaust the roots and foundation.
Thus, the Way of emperors and kings can be clearly understood.
The *Yin Pan* and *Zhou Gao* no longer leave room for doubt;
the accomplishments of past and present value practical application.
In composing literary works, one must adhere to established norms.
How could this be like a child vainly chiseling and carving?
A painted cake cannot stave off morning hunger.
Since the age of fifteen, I have applied myself diligently to the study of texts.
He ground his brushes and polished his inkstones until his spirit was exhausted;
long scrolls and large fascicles were produced in countless numbers.
His indignation was such that he desired only to support the governance of the state.
Last year, I was appointed as an official to the region south of the Zhe River.
The affairs of the bureau were so cumbersome and mundane that they could not be scrutinized;
with an open heart, I wished to emulate the brevity of Wang Jiu.
A qí-jì steed is ill-suited for catching mice;
in the great prefecture of Qiántáng, there are many high-ranking officials.
When comparing our official ranks, mine is the lowest of all.
Only Mencius alone bore the "vast and courageous qi.
Who could fold their sleeves and lower their brows forever?
What a man values most is to advance through the Way.
Ten thousand li of blue clouds must be traversed by oneself.
Alas! When I look back at myself, what am I?
I have been content to use my family’s official patronage as my own livelihood.
He then declined his illness as an excuse and withdrew far away,
suddenly casting aside his official cap and sash.
If one can admire the Master Dong of Jiaoxi, [one should follow his example].
Drawing the curtains to study with diligent austerity, he exhausted himself in the books and poetry;
dwelling in leisure and solitude, he was often moved by profound emotion.
His feelings toward contemporary governance gave rise to criticisms of its flaws.
This lowly servant, upholding his integrity,
has privately emulated [the ancients] by composing ten thousand words and presenting them at the vermilion steps.
The celestial gate, deep and secluded, lies in the northwest.
Gazing out at the vast expanse of clouds,
your virtuous voice ultimately offers no reply;
I lay bare my heart and soul in vain, shedding nothing but tears.
Alas! In my life, my destiny was perverse;
I did not encounter the leisure and ease of that time.
Like a dragon or a snake in hibernation, or a millipede in contraction.
When the myriad things do not follow their proper seasons, one must find solace within oneself.
My family’s fields and gardens lie in the southern lands;
there too are streams and mountains known as Wuyi.
The springs are sweet and the soil black, fit for sowing and reaping;
I shall return with the old farmer to attend to his plowshare.
I, Yu, was moved by these words upon hearing them.
His spirit soars and stirs, startling me as I rest my chin upon my hand;
his profound schemes and far-reaching considerations are unfathomable.
The vast ocean has no bottom, and heaven has no limit.
Before the Chāng-hé Gate, countless guests jostle shoulder to shoulder and tread foot to foot, vying to move forward;
clad in warm garments and sated with food, they indulge in their haughty pride and splendor.
How many outstanding individuals can be like this?
I ask you to step forward further so that I may speak with you;
why must you lightly discourage me when I am so earnestly striving?
The jujube ripens in winter while the hibiscus blooms at dawn;
among all things that flourish, there are those that grow quickly and those that are slow.
I have never heard of Yi Yin presenting his five petitions to Tang.
Only then can the Way of Yao and Shun be put into practice.
The worthy and eminent cast aside their own persons and value the world above all;
how could they allow themselves to be busily occupied with their private interests?
How much more so when the barbarians insult the Middle Kingdom,
trampling the two borders and overturning the very soil;
yet the General’s punitive expeditions have not yet achieved victory.
A million veteran soldiers weary their banners;
years of famine alternate with years of plenty.
Wind, rain, frost, and snow still arrive out of season.
The Son of Heaven is so diligent in his governance that he finds no leisure even for meals;
yet he also awaits those of talent to complement and assist him.
Within the temple hall, there are virtuous men.
How could one of such intelligence fail to spare the likes of Gao Yao and Shun?
Upholding the public way, he honors the Great Master;
in fashioning the *qizi* and *zizi* timber, how could there be any disparity?
Your Majesty loves me as a man of nature frank and open;
we do not criticize one another’s teachings.
Facing the wind and the bright moon, we part for a thousand li.
In offering prayers and sacrifices, how could one begrudge the pouring forth of one's very liver and spleen?
Worldly people delight in disparagement and lack joy in goodness;
take care not to let your noble reputation and pure integrity suffer any loss.
If the Imperial Court asks for the strategies of Pingjin,
who else but you could be ranked first among the worthy and good?
Ancient intent, ancient intent— five verses, one wind blowing a single speck of cloud.
Scattered as spring rain,
it sprinkles the remaining pines and cypresses;
their verdant branches are fit for gathering.
Maintaining this steadfast resolve through winter’s chill,
the hands held empty and elegant;
in the secluded valley, no one comes.
At the close of day, with whom can my mind share its thoughts?
You two, do not mock me;
this solitude is neither folly nor delusion.
Do not slight Xi Kang and Ruan Ji;
the mountain forests possess pure inspiration.
A human life lasts but a hundred years in vain.
Joy is brief, while sorrow remains;
all things, whether long or short, are but vanity.
Nothing compares to making the Way supreme.
You are not a man who haughtily spurns the world to seek renown by casting his line;
you merely decline the conditions within this realm.
Willingly I rest upon the stone steps;
in the clear sky and bright sun I soar.
Worldly affairs ultimately yield no response.
It is not as good as examining your sincerity:
speak for yourself and present it as a gift to yourself.
Three times three—within the clouds, one sees a pair of birds.
Flying high, he reveals the sun and moon;
his feathers are adorned with brilliant patterns.
Soaring and wheeling, he differs from hawks and falcons.
Tranquil and far-reaching across a thousand li,
he ultimately pays no heed to the forests and groves;
the spring breeze wafts aimlessly.
With powerful wings, you soar even more swiftly;
the gallant youths roaming the roads spy upon you in their haste.
Though there were golden pellets,
he gazed askance and did not dare to release them; from this,
one knows the value of his extraordinary qualities.
The self-preserving magpie has flown beyond;
looking back at the flock of yellow sparrows,
why do you still cling to the dust and dregs?
Four times four—how laughable! The floating clouds rise high;
they soar through the void and obscure the sun and stars. Or perhaps they are borne aloft by the *fuyao* wind.
As for the orchids and fragrant herbs, they naturally emit their sweet fragrance from within the weeds.
Self-sufficiency is a divine endowment;
there is no need for such empty spirituality.
This is what the obscured ones detest.
Why do you remain so long and solitary?
Since ancient times, those of expansive and untrammeled spirit have often left their traces in obscurity.
The mountain forests regret his long departure;
he has hidden his function and likewise hidden his form.
The valley of the ignorant is unapproachable.
Profoundly serene, he returns to his own peace;
sighing, I too envy this—
solitude and stillness to nourish my declining years.
In the fifth section on the "Exhaustion of the Five," the True Elder by chance bestowed upon me a single scroll;
deep in the forest, I encountered a reclusive person.
He left me an axe and a hoe.
What shall I do with this axe and hoe?
I shall use them to cultivate timber and vegetables.
The overgrown weeds must be pruned so that they grow lush and orderly;
what would be the purpose of bestowing books upon such a person?
I instruct your mind and body:
learning must first rectify oneself;
having governed oneself, one may then reach others.
These words contain sublime instruction;
I have worn them ever since I first received them, never once setting them aside.
How can those who drift aimlessly through life fail to heed them?
I mistakenly desire this as my own;
through mutual habituation, it has become a shallow custom.
Possessing meager virtue, I harbor a *qúhú* (a withered, hollow person).
I have composed these humble words;
I entrust them to you to transmit to others.
Visiting Daoist Master Li on Mount Youlong. As the sun rises, the wilds are vast and bright.
With solemnity he sought out Dao-sheng; then,
vanishing into the distant beyond the lakes,
he wandered freely amidst the clouds.
The autumn is high and the heavens are clear;
fallen leaves fly hither and thither.
Riding the wind, they cross over forests and ridges.
I suddenly felt my robes and sandals grow light;
at that moment, from amidst the misty distance,
a faint breeze carried the cry of a crane.
I know I am near the abode of the immortals;
my wandering thoughts become cool and pure.
In a moment, I turn into a secluded valley.
The cinnabar fields of the Purple Abode are level;
the immortal boy runs to report it,
and the pine-seed gatherer comes to welcome him at the gate.
Joining sleeves in speech and laughter,
their shared joy transcends worldly sentiment;
their rosy cheeks show they have not yet grown old.
The Way and its countenance are already perfected by Heaven.
Spreading the mats, jade-like grains are arrayed;
on the platters, purple blossoms serve as delicacies.
Our intimacy is like that of old friends;
our hearts are open and our affections poured forth.
How can I bear to depart at this fading twilight?
I linger, leaning against the mountain pillars;
I wish to make a renewed promise to seek you out again,
yet I fear it may alter your lofty reputation.
On Being Touched by Encounters, Nine Poems. I. The sea waters are clear in the dark night;
the autumn colors encompass the Penglai and Fangzhu islands.
There is an old man, a Lord of the Twin Dragons.
An iron net ensnares the coral;
wind and clouds drift vast and leisurely.
In regretful lament, what can one hope for?
I wish to ask the celestial beings:
can this bright moon be exchanged?
Two by two, the immortals dwell in the Jade Capital.
As it departs, how ethereal it becomes!
A tower of jade in twelve stories,
its latticed windows shimmering above the clouds.
The moon over the Silver River becomes its waves;
ten thousand qing become a single pond.
When autumn arrives, the palaces shine with light.
Drooping down, it falls upon the human world at dawn;
across the void, the atmosphere is at times clear and bright.
Amidst the mists and clouds, the azure birds vanish into the distance.
Visible yet unreachable;
what the mind conceives is empty and vast.
How leisurely and distant—Yang the Halberd-bearer!
His insight was far-reaching and his talent peerless;
when he first took up his brush to expound the "Mysterious" (the *Daode jing*),
he was much ridiculed by others.
The Way of Zhuangzi, Zhu Xi, Confucius, and Mencius is preeminent;
thank you for smoothing out the treacherous paths.
The jade mirror contains its subtle radiance.
In a thousand years it shall flourish once more.
Send word to those of expansive mind:
before you have attained your goal, do not lament or sigh in despair.
When the mind aspires to the Way, it is naturally noble;
worldly attitudes follow along with its momentum.
The green mountains preserve one for the long journey ahead.
Its integrity may be scrutinized even in broad daylight;
its lofty standard surpasses that of the pine and cypress.
Its solitary fragrance and steadfast character never waver.
In the four heavens where the majesty of the gods does not reach,
turmoil arises at the remote frontiers; there,
the generals exert their fierce prowess.
The momentum of heroes rises accordingly;
they emerge in profusion from Yuguang Pass,
solemnly amidst the autumn colors.
A white horse emerges through yellow clouds;
the clear frost enforces the stern decree.
The youthful warriors of the Yu-lin corps—
Strive for capability rather than excessive joy;
a love for martial prowess is not the heart of a ruler.
To employ troops is permissible only when there is no other alternative.
I address these words to the General Who Flies:
your wondrous stratagems should be peerless;
your resolve lies solely in repaying the grace of your sovereign.
How could one die for the sake of gold?
A man of honor has pledged his life to the state;
such is the spirit of noble resolve.
It would be better to have the Grand Historian record this,
rather than having Master Luan of Lu laugh it off.
Amidst the vast and boundless expanse of heaven and earth, five times five [remain].
How swift is the flow of time!
I have heard of the people of antiquity,
yet I have never seen the sun’s orb pause in its course.
Talent has sunk behind the clouds of Mount Yanzī;
it rises once more upon the Fusang tree.
The mountain colors grow dim within a world of sorrow.
The celestial form appeared in a dream at dawn;
who could have known it was King Mu?
A dragon-horse served as his divine charioteer.
Swiftly riding the wind across ten thousand li,
one proceeds once more toward the Jade Terrace;
transcending the mundane, one becomes a companion to the immortals.
For what reason should this principle not be directed toward the long life of Yao,
so as to cause him to dwell forever among mankind?
Among these sixty-six carriages and canopies, who is the traveler?
With a spirit that soars above the clouds, he is haughty;
day after day, he hastens toward the twin palace gates.
Rushing across the Wei Bridge,
golden horse trappings resound beyond the clouds;
painted candles burn within the moonlight as they traverse the ethereal celestial path.
Ascending to the Jade Canopy,
how can one within the four quarters of the world suddenly be so remote from the human realm?
She sweeps her long trailing skirt as she departs;
at the foot of the Mingguang Palace steps,
she bows once and then looks up again.
Prosperity brings much anxiety and abundance;
white hairs grow long at the temples,
and rosy cheeks wither within the mirror.
Who would have known that beneath the pines and cypresses,
the recluse remains forever silent and solitary;
with all affairs viewed as insubstantial, he is free from anxiety.
Lying at ease for long periods,
I sing out in vast freedom across heaven and earth.
Who would inquire after the Yellow Emperor Xie or Yao?
A solitary clear whistle in the breeze—
why, it is like Prince Wang Qiao!
At seventy-seven, empty and serene, he gazes upon the distant mists.
The colors of the clearing sky hold the autumnal scene;
I think of you and linger at every turn.

My gaze rests upon the peaks of a thousand mountains—my gaze, or perhaps my solitary journey—where the bright moon is perfectly full, capable of illuminating the beauty’s reflection. Whether the beauty comes or does not come, the clouds and mists stretch far across the forests and ridges.
The spirits of the eight-eight pines and cypresses on this ground cause even the weeds and brush to flourish equally;
I pray that within this domain, [peace may prevail].
The hearts of the people returned to their original purity;
in Cangwu and Kuaiji,
there were no longer any tombs or mounds.
In the six directions there is no one who understands;
on the green mountains lies the path home.
In human life, one cherishes the crimson countenance.
The worthy Zhao gazes back at me for a long time.
Last night, upon the dew-covered terrace,
who would not lament the end of autumn?
Yuan You and Yan Zileng were leisurely and at ease;
their capacities were vast and boundless.
Their old friends have now become honored sovereigns.
The white colt will surely not arrive;
he indulges in leisure and lingers by the emerald pool.
Transcending the mundane, he darts about while playing with fragrant bait.
Green mountains float white clouds;
for ten thousand ages, lofty intent is enshrined therein.
Lord Liu did not know this Way.
At first, he too felt disdain for such ambition;
why serve base kings and lords?
His mind transcends heaven and earth.
Out of pity for those such as Louhu,
why did you instead align yourself with power and influence,
wandering among the likes of Jiang and Guan?
Bending my willow-like frame, I stagger along the path;
the Way of the Ancient Sovereigns is vast and bright,
yet this weary life binds me fast.
It is better to return home;
riding the wind, I wave my long sleeves.
Missing the region of Yue and addressing the various bodhisattvas of Shanyin: weary of seeing the clamor of human realms.
In this pure excursion, I recall Lingyue:
to the southeast lie tens of thousands of mountains,
their drifting azure filling the vast, silent void.
The scenery within this mirror has long been a marvel;
its topographical excellence is peerless among men.
The moon is so clear it transforms the Goose River.
Clouds rise from the Cave of Stored Books;
like a traveler adrift on a tumbleweed,
I am suddenly parted from my old friend.
Before this letter on silk could be delivered,
the fragrant herbs have already withered.
What I lament is the difficulty of the traveler's path.
Bending and bowing, one’s reputation and integrity are diminished.
As the wild geese prepare to fly eastward,
I send this message to the bright moon.
An Autumn Eve Verse: In the mountain home last night, the chambers grew cold;
A single leaf of wutong drifted into the golden well.
The vast sky was like clear water, hidden from the clouds.
The bright moon contains its radiance as the autumnal scene transforms;
The cassia branches unfold their blossoms as the wind wafts lightly.
Who atop the high tower blows the jade flute?
On earth, people do not see the raft ascending to the Milky Way;
in the heavens, they shall soon behold the magpies forming a bridge.
Where, then, are the young soldiers on their campaign?
The white dew drenches my clothes, yet I have not yet returned;
by the seashore, there is now no house for a wandering mother.
In Jiangnan, who will encounter this prince?
Pacing back and forth beneath the moon, I chant long and deep.
Among our kind, it has been difficult from of old to find one who understands.
I wish to ascend the high terrace and question the bright moon.
Why does the bright moon not illuminate the human heart?
The Assembly of Worthies Staying at the Mountain Compose a Poem on "Dwelling Beneath the Cliff in the Evening Clouds": A gentle breeze stills the treetops.
The crimson sun descends upon the rocky slopes;
the bright moon has already risen full,
yet the white clouds have not yet returned in great numbers.
High, he should keep company with monkeys and cranes;
deep, he shall not be obscured by pines and creepers.
If you do not depart to become the rain-bringing dragon, [what else can you do?]
What can be done about such a drought?
Gazing at the evening view of the Zhejiang River: the twilight stretches boundlessly;
the autumn sky and the waters merge with heaven.
A single sail flies beyond the soaring birds;
the new moon descends at the edge of the tide.
The mountain shapes appear small from this distance.
The terrain of the swallowed Wu region is biased;
how many have grown old coming and going?
When will the boat at the ferry crossing arrive?
Inscription on Jing Mountain Temple Its verdant peaks thrust upward beyond the surrounding mountains;
its soaring momentum toward the heavens never ceases.
Clouds obscure the path of flying birds.
The rain emerges from the ancient dragon pool;
the monk dwells in deep clouds in meditative concentration.
Fragrance blends with the misty haze and drifts upward.
Mortals cannot reach its heights;
the terraces and halls are naturally serene in autumn.
Minister Lang, having retired from office—Minister Lang, having retired from office—was always uniquely lofty in his withdrawal from the world.
The Way surpasses desire, so he conceals his brilliance;
with white hair, he takes leave of his sovereign lord.
Amidst green mountains, he cherishes his native land.
The medicinal garden allows cranes to enter;
I fear the clouds may hide the path for reciting poetry.
I cherish even more lying within the Zen grove.
At times I come to sweep the stone bed.
Among the mountains, the early plum blossoms—the early plum blossoms among the mountains—stand tall, reflecting the evening light;
their pure whiteness emerges from the treetops.
A small garden stretches into the distant clouds;
solitary blossoms brave the cold of the snow.
Such a sight is yet rarely seen among men.
One should first look upon it as something beyond the mundane;
one merely desires it to be like square jade,
for how could it compare to the excellence of the peony?
Floating on the Yue River at the Ruo Ye Creek: Floating on the Yue River in springtime, The boat windows are closed and then opened again.
Beautiful mountains pass by along the banks.
Sudden rain brings falling blossoms;
the reflection of the bank shows a woodcutter crossing;
the sound of singing brings a washerwoman back.
The Canglang River holds boundless meaning;
as evening falls, it becomes even more serene.
Inscribed at Ma Youzhang’s Garden Pavilion. I cherish the excellence of this garden and grove.
Returning again, the flowers and trees flourish;
travelers become so intoxicated they cannot depart.
The warbling of the secluded birds knows no end.
The smoky city walls border the lush green grass;
the spring lakes overflow into the emerald pools.
The pines and bamboos possess no vulgar air.
The traveler idly awaits your arrival.
At evening on the mountain pavilion, the spring evening is still;
the forest rocks stand naturally craggy.
The dog leaves to bark at the words of men;
flowers fly freely as birds catch them in their beaks;
clear smoke perfumes the lush grass.
The warm sun mingles with the misty tall pines;
even more joyful is the full moon.
Its pure light descends upon the azure cliffs.
A gift for myself, a gift for myself: sitting in stillness, I gaze at the bamboo;
wandering idly, I join the woodcutters.
The Way-seeking mind must surely reside within.
Life's affairs have become devoid of concern;
guests depart and refined conversation is scarce;
as the years pass, white hairs abound.
Carelessly employing the brush of Zhi Dun,
I idly compose this "Xiaoyao" (Recluse) poem:
On a summer day without rain— on a summer day without rain, there is truly no rain in the mountains.
Day after day we gaze upon the clouds and rainbows;
from Lesser Heat comes Greater Heat.
The deep ravines have become shallow streams.
The springs have dried up down to the bottoms of the wells;
the earth is so parched with heat that the vegetable plots are withered.
There is nothing with which to question the will of Heaven.
Vainly I think of the water-birds crying; the common saying is that when the water-birds cry, it rains throughout the world.
Writing of My Feelings at the End of the Year: At the end of the year, I write of my thoughts as the northern wind suddenly turns cold.
The morning sun is about to shed its warmth,
yet I have not yet returned from the southern lands;
on Mount Dong, the year draws to a close.
This ephemeral life passes away in an instant;
how could one’s fragrant countenance be made to stay?
I send this message of thanks to those in the world of men.
The profusion of worldly splendors is all the more worthy of awakening.
Traveling early in the mountains—traveling early in the mountains—the front peaks have been soaked by night rain;
I go alone, treading through the spring mud.
The sun is about to rise over the celestial horizon;
the roosters of the farming households crow once more.
A solitary plume of smoke rises wherever one travels.
The wilderness stretches low into the distance;
I am still glad to have encountered this woodcutter.
Together we shall cross several streams.
Returning Late from the Lake: Having finished my brief excursion among men, I follow my inclination for reclusion back toward my old retreat;
walking along the spring bank, I have not yet reached its end.
The setting sun seems about to vanish;
the misty mountains grow faint at the horizon.

I now place the *Record of Deeds* compiled by Lingju at the beginning of this volume,
so that one may clearly perceive the lineage of the Master’s ancestry and the traces of his emergence in the world and his subsequent departure.
His extraordinary conduct, noble deeds, eminent talent, and superior virtue established a style that transcended his age. Thus,
he compiled the *Fujiao bian* (Compilation for Assisting the Teaching) into three volumes— upper, middle, and lower— as the first part,

His aspiration was to harmonize Confucianism and Buddhism to guide the scholar-officials;

and realize their true nature, thereby silencing the clamor of jealousy, slander, and disputes over right and wrong.

Furthermore, I have appended the "Treatise on the Ultimate Truth" (Zhendi wusheng lun) to the end of the "Eulogy on the Platform Sutra" within the *Fujiao bian* (Compilation for Assisting the Teachings),
in order to manifest that the Master’s intent lay in propagating and extolling the unsurpassed, supreme, subtle, profound, and vast Way of our Buddha, the Great Sage.
It does not reside in written words or spoken language.
The meaning of what is called the "separate transmission outside the teachings" is likely to be seen in this work.
Thus, its concluding eulogy says:
The Dharma is shown to be beyond words and letters;
therefore, the tradition of the Perfected Ones values silent transmission.
It is further said:
The Sage is like spring, which brings forth all things in a state of vibrant abundance;
the Perfected Person is like autumn, which completes all things in a state of pure clarity.
This is what is meant by saying that, in the end, one returns to stillness and silence.
Therefore, the conclusion of the *Wu sheng lun* (Treatise on the Absence of Sages) regarding ultimate truth states:
"The perceptions of ordinary beings and sages are merely the shadows of ultimate truth and the攀缘 (pān-yuan—
clinging and seeking) of the deluded mind."
Nevertheless, those who are devoted to the study of foreign scripts—
upon reading these two accounts—
will they not be somewhat alerted within their own minds?
The previous edition of this *Fujiao ji* (Collection for Assisting the Teachings) had been repeatedly carved into printing blocks;
consequently, although it was widely circulated in the world,
there were approximately sixty or more places where the text and meaning were corrupted or erroneous.
Now, all of these have been verified and corrected by means of the canonical scriptures.

In Praise of the Great Master Zhanmingjiao; A Preface to the Account of Cultivating Stillness at Tianzhu Mountain in Longshu. I have read the *Fujiaobian* (Compilation for Assisting the Teaching) by Chan Master Song. It states: "The Buddha-dharma has been transmitted from India to China. This is because the Dharma-body is originally non-dual, yet it manifests as two distinct bodies: the Dharma-body and the Reward-body. Furthermore, it is said that the Dharma-body is formless, while the Reward-body possesses form. Moreover, the Dharma-body is without speech, whereas the Reward-body speaks. Thus, the Dharma-body is the essence, and the Reward-body is its function. The Dharma-body is the principle, and the Reward-body is its manifestation. The Dharma-body is the cause, and the Reward-body is the fruit. The Dharma-body is the internal, and the Reward-body is the external. The Dharma-body is the absolute truth, and the Reward-body is the conventional truth. The Dharma-body is the ultimate, and the Reward-body is the provisional.
